title: bonsai.asks/1
description: bonsai ask, bonsai ask --resolve, bonsai ask --status, bonsai answer and bonsai asks, with --json (contract §9, spec §4, §8, §16 row 30): the asks a command read, each key with its state, and the record the command appended. Printed, never stored (the asks themselves are the ask records, bonsai.ask/1, in the main checkout's .bonsai/local/asks/). Written by those commands with --json; read by agents, the studio's bridge and CI, now that Bonsai has no screens of its own. An ask's state follows its records: open until an answer record or a resolve record for its key closes it, then answered or resolved. The records inside are bonsai.ask/1's, as stored; they are open objects here, because the schema checker has no $ref and a full copy would refuse an older or hand-written record, so bonsai.ask/1 is their home. When the command refuses before it reads a workspace (exit 2 or 4), workspace is null, asks is [] and error says why. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null, [] or {} where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version, always the first field (contract §2.2).

workspace.description: The workspace: its id and name from bonsai.yaml, and the checkout's absolute path, forward slashes (printed locally, never stored or forwarded); null when the command stopped before reading bonsai.yaml.

root.description: The checkout's absolute path, forward slashes.

asks.description: The asks the command read, each a key with its state: for ask --status, asks and answer, the key or keys asked about; for ask and ask --resolve, the key filed or resolved. Sorted by the time of their latest file record, then key. [] for none, and when the command refused.

filed.title: Which colour should the dark theme use for links?
filed.why: The design file gives two blues and the contrast check passes for both.
filed.then_text: The builder applies the chosen colour and reruns the contrast check.

state.description: Where the ask stands, a closed list: open (no answer and no resolve record yet), answered (an answer record closed it) or resolved (the asker withdrew it with a resolve record).

filed.description: The key's latest file record, as stored (bonsai.ask/1, which is its home); an open object here.

examples.title: Which colour should the dark theme use for links?
examples.why: The design file gives two blues and the contrast check passes for both.
examples.then_text: The builder applies the chosen colour and reruns the contrast check.

closed.description: The answer or resolve record that closed the ask, as stored (bonsai.ask/1); null while it is open.

written.description: The ask record this run appended (a file, resolve or answer record, as stored: bonsai.ask/1); null when the run wrote none (asks, ask --status, or a refusal).

examples.title: Does the new settings screen read well in the dark theme?
examples.why: A person has to look at it; the screenshots pass the contrast check.
examples.then_text: The builder moves the task to verify.

error.description: null unless the command refused or failed: then what went wrong and the next step, as bonsai.error has it.

examples.message: bonsai.yaml is not in this checkout, so it is not linked to Bonsai

next.do: run: bonsai init in the project's main checkout

code.description: What went wrong, as a fixed word: an open list (contract §2.2). Later steps add words, which is an addition (format review 4.5), and a reader shows a word it does not know as other. The known words live in one table in Bonsai's code, their one home, which bonsai check --schema bonsai.error prints (and, from step 5.1.10, the reference page of lists, docs/reference/lists.md); this schema does not copy them, and the words in its examples are illustrative.

message.description: What is wrong, one sentence for a person, in ASCII (spec §3).
examples: no --yes, and no terminal to ask at: nothing was written

next.description: The next thing to do (spec §3: every refusal and error names it, in the human line and in the JSON): what to do and who does it.

do.description: What to do: the command to run, written run: and the command line, or the step in plain words.
examples: open Claude Code in this checkout and accept its trust question

who.description: Who does it, a closed list: agent (any agent may do it, unattended) or person (a person's step: a consent such as --allow-exec, a tap, a setting, an install, or a command an agent's task does not grant it; spec §4, §6).
